thread:
maria.chen: Quick question — we need a lightweight decision-tree for routing requests to FP8/INT8/4-bit paths and when to trigger a quality fallback. Sketching options here, want ops + runtime input.
ajay.singh: +1. do you mean per-request heuristics or per-endpoint?
maria.chen: Per-request (customer SLOs vary) but with per-endpoint defaults. goal: maximize cost savings while bounding quality regressions to X% for high-tier customers.
tyler.h: We also need telemetry signals that are cheap to compute on the hot path. latency budget is tight.
sophia.k: Suggestion: two-stage check. 1) static profile (endpoint-level): allowed bitwidths + expected degradation threshold. 2) fast runtime probe: token-level logp delta or prefix-consistency score. if probe fails -> fallback.
ajay.singh: How do we compute the probe without full decode? we can't run 2x model evals.
maria.chen: think of fast approximations: a single-token scoring pass (next-token logp) using the low-bit variant, compared to stored baseline stats. treat sudden logp drop relative to baseline stdev as signal.
tyler.h: Example metric: delta_logp_z = (logp_lowbit - mean_baseline)/std_baseline. if < -2 then flag. cheap and O(1) per request.
sophia.k: Need to account for prompt drift across customers. baseline should be maintained per-customer or per-endpoint sample window (rolling).
ajay.singh: Telemetry: we should emit sample-level tags: "probe_delta_z", "precision_used", "fallback_reason". Keep histogram buckets for delta_z.
maria.chen: Ops question: how many false positives can we tolerate? Fallbacks cost more. For low-tier endpoints maybe tolerate more FPs.
tyler.h: We can gate by customer tier in routing policy — e.g., aggressive low-bit for tier C, conservative for tier A. but core decision API should be the same.
sophia.k: UX for operators: expose per-endpoint tradeoff sliders (cost vs quality). store as (allowed_lowbits, z_threshold, sample_rate).
ajay.singh: Implementation concerns: where lives the baseline stats? cheap store in redis per-endpoint with a TTL + async re-accumulation job. must be readable at <1ms.
maria.chen: Agree. Also need periodic calibration job that runs full-eval on held-out prompts to detect drift and update mean/std.
tyler.h: Edge-case: adversarial prompts can spoof low-bit probe but still yield ok semantics. we should augment with a small set of high-value eval prompts for each endpoint that are checked at sample_rate 0.1% as a stronger signal.
sophia.k: Good idea — mix fast probe + sparse gold checks. golden checks can be run asynchronously and trigger rollback if quality degr > threshold.
ajay.singh: Telemetry schema proposal (cheap):
```
probe_delta_z: float
precision: string  # e.g., fp8,int8,4bit
fallback: bool
fallback_type: string # probe|error|capacity
sample_type: string # fast_probe|gold_check
```
Keep fields minimal.
maria.chen: Can we avoid per-request baseline lookups by approximating mean/std with an exponential moving average locally in the runtime instance? saves redis read but means stats are instance-local.
tyler.h: Tradeoff: local EMA -> faster, but split-brain stats across instances may increase variance. but for a z-threshold heuristic it's probably fine; we just need conservative thresholds.
sophia.k: For dedicated customers we should prefer centralized baselines (accurate) and for hosted scale use local EMA. document these as two operational modes.
ajay.singh: Rollout plan: 1) implement probe + EMA locally, 2) expose per-endpoint config, 3) run A/B with gold checks logging, 4) after baseline stabilization switch on redis-backed central stats for high-tier endpoints.
maria.chen: Action items: @ajay.singh draft runtime API for probe check + config schema. @tyler.h scope perf impact (p99 extra ns). @sophia.k outline operator console controls + telemetry panels. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with graphs.
tyler.h: I'll run microbenchmarks today and post numbers.
ajay.singh: I'll prototype API shape — thinking: decide_precision(request_meta, probe_result) -> {precision, reason_tags}. keep deterministic and idempotent.
sophia.k: Also add an opt-out header for customers who want fixed precision pins.
maria.chen: Thanks folks. one more note — we should log sample ids when golden checks fail so we can replay and improve quant profiles.
runtime-bot: Deploy scheduled: quant-probe-experiment v0.1 -> staging at 2024-09-12T03:00Z :rocket:
maria.chen: ack, will comment on RFC with the experiment plan and expected metrics (cost delta, fallback rate, quality delta).
ajay.singh: +1. keeping this small and reversible is key.
summary: Quick thread to align on a runtime decision-tree for low-bit routing with cheap probes, telemetry schema, and rollout plan
